Maria: quick sync — profiling showed a reproducible perf regression after switching to per-channel FP8 kernels for the llama-family build. small-batch throughput down ~18%, tail latency up.
Raj: hmm, is the KV-cache hit rate changing? or is it more kernel scheduling overhead?
Maria: initial logs point to more KV cache invalidations on reuse patterns. looks like different quant layouts change memory alignment -> more L2 spills. attached run: `perf record` snapshots.
Tim: can you paste the hot stack from `perf top`? curious if GEMM kernel changed or if memcpy dominates.
Maria: here: ```
# perf top -p 1423
12.3%  libredwood_gemm.so  gemm_fp8_pchan
10.1%  libcudart.so       memcpy
8.7%   libredwood_kv.so   kv_lookup
6.5%   libredwood_gemm.so  gemm_int8_fallback
```
Anya: memcpy jump is telling. per-channel layout might be scattering weights which increases reads. also see `kv_lookup` tick up, maybe due to cache line alignment.
Raj: did you try per-tensor FP8 for the same model? if perf is better we can treat per-channel as a quality-only opt in.
Maria: per-tensor FP8 baseline: throughput is +14% vs per-channel FP8. accuracy drop is model-dependent (some heads slip ~0.2-0.4 ppl). tradeoff there.
Jess: could batch heuristics be masking this? small batches are most affected. what if we increase batching window or enable mini-batching within single request?
Tim: good call. adding a short batching delay (5-10ms) reduced memcpy saturation and recovered ~9% throughput in tests.
Anya: but that increases P50 slightly. we need an SLO decision: prefer throughput for background jobs, p50 for interactive.
perf-bot: perf-run 1755567901 completed. artifact: s3://redwood-perf/17555679/fp8-perf-compare.tar.gz
Raj: thinking of a hybrid policy: default to per-tensor FP8 on hosted endpoints for edge latency, allow per-channel FP8 for dedicated heavy-throughput endpoints where we can tune batching.
Maria: also proposal: during calibration stage, detect "spectral outliers" (weights with >X sigma) and force per-tensor quant for those layers to avoid strided scatters and alignment penalties.
Jess: interesting — treat outlier layers with per-tensor or higher precision (int8) and rest per-channel. need a fast detector in the compile path.
Tim: compiler can add a pass: compute per-layer variance histogram from calibration set and mark layers. overhead negligible if we cache results per model-version.
Raj: calibration dataset matters — if we pick too many short-chat prompts we bias KV reuse patterns. suggest mixing longer context samples to represent LLM app behavior.
Anya: +1. also include synthetic tail sequences that stress KV churn (many distinct keys) to reveal alignment issues.
Maria: action items: 1) run per-channel vs per-tensor perf matrix across 4 batch sizes; 2) add mini-batching tweak experiment; 3) prototype spectral-outlier detector in compile; 4) update calibration corpus to include KV-churn traces.
Jess: I'll own the cal-corpus change. pushing a PR with sampling heuristic today.
Raj: I'll run the perf matrix on dedicated infra and post results here.
Maria: thanks. if anyone wants to jump on a quick call to triage the code paths, ping me. :phone: :eyes:
Anya: adding a note — capture `nvprof` memcopy timeline for the worst-case run so we can show kernel vs copy time.
Tim: and collect `pmap` to sanity-check addr alignment after quantization transform.
Maria: noted. will attach artifacts when runs finish.
Jess: (thumbsup)
